newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Loss of faith in courts worries Manila.
newsitem.headline: Loss of faith in courts worries Manila.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos voiced concern on Wednesay over possible loss of people's faith in the Philippine justice system after the controversial acquittal of a politician in a murder trial.
He said he had ordered steps to be taken to improve the quality of state prosecutors after the prosecution in the trial of mayor Honorato Galvez was criticised for mishandling the case.
A local court on Tuesday acquitted Galvez of murder charges in a case involving a young man whom he and his bodyguard allegedly shot and killed in a 1993 land dispute.
A brother and an uncle of the victim were also shot and wounded in the incident which occurred in nearby San Ildefonso town where Galvez has been mayor for eight years.
The judge found the bodyguard guilty and sentenced him to life in jail but said the prosecution failed to produce enough evidence to show Galvez ordered and took part in the killing.
The victims' families, their lawyers and citizens groups slammed the mayor's acquittal and warned it would destroy popular confidence in the judicial system.
The case drew national attention because of perceptions that the country's elite are above the law.
Ramos said he had ordered three senior cabinet ministers, including the justice secretary, the presidential palace chief of staff and the presidential legal counsel to study the trial's proceedings.
"I asked (them) ... to determine what can be done to prevent the erosion of the people's confidence in our justice system," Ramos told his weekly news conference.
The Citizens Action Against Crime, a group which monitors government handling of the crime situation, warned loss of public confidence in the courts "will drive people to seek justice their own way."
"A demoralised citizenry who take the law into their own hands can only breed anarchy in our streets," the group said.
